summary: Robeson County tower erected 1934 by the CCC at 99 ft 9 in; its grounds were closed to visitors without a Forest Service representative in 1954. Current status not found.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
facts.status_note: No source found says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: Steel tower of 99 ft 9 in, erected by the CCC, per the lookout-history page.

April 15, 1954 Robesonian report, as quoted by the lookout-history page: grounds declared off limits to anyone not accompanied by a State Forest Service representative, after damage to signs and posts.

evidence.supports: 1934 steel tower of 99 ft 9 in erected by the CCC
evidence.quote: 1934: A 99-foot 9-inch steel tower was erected by the CCC.

evidence.supports: agency is the NC Division of Forest Resources
evidence.quote: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: April 15, 1954 Robesonian report: grounds declared off limits unless accompanied by a Forest Service representative
evidence.quote: April 15, 1954: County Forest Ranger Braddie Pait and Forest Service officials have declared the property at the Proctorville fire tower off limits to anyone not accompanied by some representative of the N.C. State Forest Service.

evidence.supports: Pait, as quoted in the report, said the grounds were left unfit for legitimate visitors
evidence.quote: the grounds have been rendered entirely unpresentable to legitimate visitors

evidence.supports: report apparently blames young boys for destroying signs and knocking down posts
evidence.quote: apparently young boys of the show-off variety are responsible for destroying official signs and knocking down posts.

evidence.supports: list places Proctorville tower in Robeson County at 34.496 N, 79.032 W

corrections.why: The lookout-history page gives 99 feet 9 inches, which is about 30.4 m. 30.2 m is closer to 99 feet with the 9 inches dropped.

notes_for_editor: The 1934 build line on the lookout-history page names no source. The 1954 Robesonian article is known only as quoted there. Current access is unknown: the 1954 closure is historical, and no source says whether it was lifted, so no access key is recorded. Status, staffing and fires are unsourced. The 30.2 m brief height is corrected to 30.4 m (99 ft 9 in). Not on the NHLR North Carolina list or the FFLOS North Carolina list.
